$comment: Upstream of every vendored extension. Managed by scripts/upstream.mjs (status / diff / pull / check). commit = the upstream commit vendor/<dest> is based on; localChanges = what this repository changed on top of it.

localChanges: Vendored from the unreleased v2.0.0 on main (npm still ships 1.1.6).
spawn.ts/bash.ts: a foreground command keeps its child ref'd, so headless `pi -p` no longer exits on the first bash call; it is unref'd once it moves to the background.

timeout-policy.ts (new), bash.ts, bash-params.ts: foreground commands move to the background after 30s by default and at most 60s (PI_PRESET_BASH_BG_DEFAULT / PI_PRESET_BASH_BG_CAP, `off` = upstream timing); the timeout parameter and a bash guideline say it backgrounds rather than kills.
src/__tests__/preset-local.test.ts (new): tests for both changes, including a headless keepAlive repro.

tools/{bash,bash-bg,jobs,monitor,agent-bg}.ts: prompt guidelines deduplicated and condensed (sleep / one-vs-per-event / jobs actions were repeated across tools); jobs actions described once in its description.

tools/bash.ts, output.ts, types.ts: a foreground command reports an empty partial result at once and streams its log from the start every 250ms (upstream: nothing for 2s, then 1s polls), so pi's bash renderer shows the live Elapsed clock and output for quiet commands too.

registry.ts, spawn.ts, monitor-ws.ts: job logs go to a per-user <tmpdir>/pi-bg-<uid> directory (0700, owner and symlink checked) with 0600 files; upstream used a shared world-readable /tmp/pi-bg that any local user could read or pre-create.

shell.ts (new), spawn.ts, monitor-source.ts, tools/{bash,bash-bg,monitor}.ts: `command` spawns run in the shell from pi's exported getShellConfig with the session's shellPath (pi.getSettings(): project .pi/settings.json over the global file), writing the command to stdin for commandTransport "stdin" shells; upstream ran `bash -c` through a PATH lookup, which ignored shellPath and on Windows with WSL picked C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe ahead of Git Bash, which exits 1 with an empty log when detached with file output, so every bash / bash_bg / monitor call returned "(no output yet)". `file` spawns (agent_bg) are unchanged.

spawn.ts: killProcessTree kills the whole tree on Windows with System32 taskkill /F /T (process.kill(-pid) has no process groups there and only the shell died); POSIX is unchanged. Children get windowsHide.
src/__tests__/shell.test.ts (new): shellPath is used by spawn and by bash / monitor, stdin transport, a simulated Windows PATH with System32\bash.exe first, and taskkill.

tools/bash-bg.ts and src/__tests__/bash-bg.test.ts removed, index.ts no longer registers bash_bg: it duplicated bash run_in_background=true. sleep-guard.test.ts now drives bash run_in_background; README marks the tool as removed.

check-in.ts (new), types.ts, lifecycle.ts, tools/{bash,bash-params,agent-bg,jobs}.ts: bash and agent_bg take expected_seconds; a background job still running past it (then 2x, 4x, at least 30s apart; default PI_PRESET_BG_CHECK=300, off disables) sends the agent a statusless <task-notification> check-in with elapsed time, last output change, and log tail (steer + triggerTurn). A jobs attach following the job returns with the check-in instead and leaves the completion notification armed. Upstream only warned for y/n-style prompt tails, so a job that never exits left the agent waiting and an attach held the turn until Esc. src/__tests__/check-in.test.ts (new).
tools/jobs.ts: attach holds the event loop while it waits (a ref'd no-op interval); every job and timer is unref'd, so headless pi -p exited mid-attach and orphaned the job.
Lives inside vendor/pi-workspace-history: /fuck rewinds through navigateTree, which workspace-history intercepts to offer restoring the files too.
Only the TypeScript extension is vendored; the native search library stays an npm dependency (@ff-labs/fff-node, pinned in the root package.json).
src/index.ts: grep/find guidelines condensed, shared path/exclude parameter descriptions shortened; multi_grep (off by default) untouched.

todo.ts, tool/types.ts: guidelines condensed from 9 rules to 2 and the description/field texts shortened; batch create (tasks[], v2.15) is a clause in the tool description plus one item-field description instead of a ninth guideline and long field texts; behavior unchanged.

tool/types.ts, state/state-reducer.ts: owner and metadata removed from the tool schema (top level and tasks[] items) and from the update error text; Task, replay, and the reducer still accept them, so older sessions that set them replay unchanged.
ask-user-question.ts, tool/types.ts: tool description, guidelines, and schema field descriptions condensed (~1.8k → ~0.4k tokens); the limits stay enforced by the schema and validator.
Shared library for the two rpiv extensions; resolved through a file: dependency in the root package.json.
package.json: typebox moved from dependencies to peerDependencies (pi provides it; the bundled copy triggered a startup warning).

mcp/tools.py: no tool takes or returns a secret. login, login_complete, and logout are removed (sign-in is /termius login in pi, through json_login.py); sync has no password argument; inventory lists snippet labels only.
mcp/tools.py + redact.py (new): every tool result and error is scrubbed of vault secrets (identity passwords, key passphrases, private keys, the vault password) and any PEM private key block.
core/ssh_exec.py: host keys are pinned on first use in ~/.termius/known_hosts (TERMIUS_KNOWN_HOSTS); a changed key is refused. Upstream used AutoAddPolicy.

json_login.py (new) + main.py: `termius login-json` reads one JSON request on stdin (email / google / status / logout) and answers otp_required / approve_required, so pi can drive sign-in without argv, env, or the model.
mcp/server.py, sync.py, vault.py: messages point at /termius login instead of the removed login tool.
tests/unit: login-tool tests replaced; preset_local_test.py (new) covers the changes above.

json_login.py: a successful sign-in pulls the inventory with the password it was given (a failed pull is reported, not fatal); new `sync` action pulls with the remembered vault password. mcp/tools.py: `status` pulls once when signed in but never synced. Upstream signed in without syncing, so status showed 0 hosts until a host tool ran.

Jump hosts and proxies: transformers/many.py keeps Termius hostchain_set on the ssh_config rows (local-only `host_chain` field, never pushed); ssh_merge.get_jump_route resolves host and group chains (a first jump host's own chain first, loops refused); ssh_exec.connect_host chains paramiko connections over direct-tcpip channels, each hop with its own credentials and pinned key; core/proxy.py adds SOCKS5/SOCKS4/HTTP CONNECT for hosts without a chain (TERMIUS_MCP_PROXY from pi's /termius proxy, else ALL_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY with NO_PROXY). host shows jump_hosts, proxy, and ssh -J; exec reports its route.

mcp/server.py: a watchdog thread exits the server once its client process is gone (parent changes), so a request in progress (a long exec) no longer keeps the server and its SSH connections alive after pi was killed. It runs next to upstream's threaded StdioServer (3.2.0), which on end of stdin waits for running calls, each capped by its own timeout.

core/ssh_exec.py, ssh_files.py (3.2.0 merge): upstream's whole-call deadline, polling reader, and cancel token are combined with the local pinned host keys, jump host chains, and proxies. Every hop is resolved to a plain SshTarget under runtime.lock (connect_host(target, route=[SshTarget, ...], cancel, deadline); run_file_action takes route too); each hop's connect stages are capped by the call deadline and registered with the cancel token, so a timeout or cancel closes the whole chain. Upstream 3.2.0 still uses AutoAddPolicy and has no route.
core/ssh_exec.py: pinning a new host key is serialized with a lock, since tool calls now run in threads.
mcp/tools.py: _ssh_target_for returns (target, route); call_tool also holds runtime.lock while it reads the vault secrets for redaction.

tests/unit: route_test.py moved to SshTarget hops and adds a cancel mid-chain, deadline-capped hops, and exec resolving the chain then running without the lock; upstream tools_test.py's fake run_host_command accepts route; preset_local_test.py skips parsing its fixture key, which is now parsed before the (mocked) SSH call.

policy.py (new): per-host settings from pi's /termius, read from config.json (TERMIUS_MCP_POLICY) whenever it changes, failing closed when unreadable. hosts.<cloud id>.level == off hides a host from hosts (reported as hidden) and refuses host/exec/files with host_disabled; it still works as a jump host. Route modes termius / termius-proxy / direct / proxy, globally and per host, plus a per-host proxy URL; a route that needs a missing proxy is route_unavailable, never a direct fallback.

core/ssh_exec.py: connect_host takes the first-connection proxy explicitly (AUTO_PROXY keeps the old rule) and reports each connected hop through on_stage; run_host_command and ssh_files.run_file_action pass proxy through; files results carry route. mcp/tools.py: _ssh_target_for returns (target, hops, proxy) along the host's route; host rows carry cloud_id, tags, and route; hosts and the query filter cover tags; tool descriptions mention access levels, hidden hosts, and routes.

json_login.py: `hosts` lists every host for pi's menu (disabled ones too, with the cloud ids its route goes through, optional pull when older than 10 minutes) and `test` connects along a host's route hop by hop, authenticating and running nothing; neither returns a secret. tests/unit/policy_test.py (new) covers policy.py, routes, disabled hosts, and both actions; the fake run_host_command in route_test.py and tools_test.py accepts proxy.
